title: The use of environmental DNA metabarcoding in the evaluation of vertebrate communities across urban stream restoration gradients
description: In the present study, an eDNA metabarcoding approach was utilized to survey vertebrate communities found in seven sites that have undergone varying types of ecological restoration as well as minimally disturbed and degraded reference sites in an urban area centered in Lexington, Kentucky, USA. A total of 71 vertebrate taxa were detected, including 34 fish species as well as amphibian, reptile, bird, and mammal taxa. Pairwise comparisons of restored/non-restored sites revealed some site-specific increases in species richness and relative read abundance in restored areas but not in pooled comparisons. However, pooled fish and amphibian analyses as well as non-metric multidimensional scaling, clearly differentiated minimally disturbed and degraded urban sites. Additionally, an eDNA-based fish IBI was utilized, using both raw metrics and the Kentucky IBIs drainage-area-scaled scoring framework, to assess the ecological condition. Significant differences were detected in raw IBI metrics, whereas drainage-scaled scores attenuated these differences.
